rows.grounds: ablative sense from union with that

items.question: What transformation arises from union with that supreme reality?
premises: Union with that reality produces a change in the practitioner.
The transformed practitioner becomes a kaula.
The transformed practitioner attains the status of a divine hero.
items.inference: Therefore union with that reality elevates one to the kaula divine-hero state.
items.plain_english: O great goddess, through union with that, one became a kaula and a divine hero.

rows.grounds: negated suitability as yogin for us
injunction to worship addressed to goddess
vocative address to goddess of kula

items.question: Who is fit to worship when seeking liberation in the kula path?
premises: One merely equally united is not the yogin meant here.
The seeker addressed desires liberation.
Such a seeker should perform worship.
items.inference: Therefore the liberation-seeker must worship rather than remain merely equally united.
uncertainties: The exact force of 'no' in 'sa no yogī bhaved' is contextually compressed.
items.plain_english: O goddess, beloved of the kula, one who is merely equally united would not be our yogin; the one desiring liberation should worship.

items.question: What contemplative identification is prescribed if one can perform it?
premises: The self can be taken as the object of contemplation.
The supreme brahman is presented as that object.
Contemplation is offered as an alternative condition.
items.inference: Therefore one should contemplate oneself as the supreme brahman, if able.
items.plain_english: One should contemplate oneself as the supreme brahman, or if not.

rows.grounds: the teaching designated as divine yoga

items.question: How must the teaching of divine yoga be protected?
premises: This teaching is identified as divine yoga.
The goddess is directly instructed regarding it.
Guarding is to be done with attentiveness.
items.inference: Therefore this divine yoga must be guarded carefully.
items.plain_english: O goddess, guard this divine yoga with attentiveness.

rows.grounds: qualified by the power of kalā

items.question: What initial object should be contemplated in this meditative sequence?
premises: A triad of drops is specified as the object.
This triad is pervaded by kalā.
It is to be contemplated first.
items.inference: Therefore the first contemplation is the kalā-pervaded triad of drops.
items.plain_english: First one should contemplate the triad of drops pervaded by kalā.

rows.grounds: light filling all directions and space

items.question: What luminous quality characterizes the contemplated bindu triad?
premises: The radiance is compared to crores of rising suns.
This radiance illuminates the directions and space.
Both descriptions qualify the contemplated form.
items.inference: Therefore the bindu triad is contemplated as supremely radiant and all-illuminating.
items.plain_english: It shines with the radiance of crores of young suns, illuminating the directions and space.

rows.grounds: middle bodily region defined by bindu extent
bodily span from throat region to hip and head

items.question: Which bodily region corresponds to the middle bindu in contemplation?
premises: The middle body is related to the extent of the bindu.
The region is specified from throat to hip and head.
This defines the locus for contemplation.
items.inference: Therefore the middle bindu is contemplated in the central bodily region spanning throat, hip, and head.
uncertainties: The exact anatomical mapping of 'kaṭiśīrṣakam' is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Contemplate the middle body up to the bindu as extending from the throat to the hip and head.

rows.grounds: lower region starting from the womb
extent reaching down to the feet

items.question: What further bodily extents must be included in the bindu contemplation?
premises: A region beginning with the womb is specified.
Its extent reaches down to the feet.
Another limit is described as ending at desire.
items.inference: Therefore contemplation must include these specified lower and desire-related extents.
uncertainties: The precise referent of 'kāmāntaṃ' in this bodily mapping is unclear.
items.plain_english: One should contemplate the region beginning with the womb and ending at the feet, and extending up to the limit of desire.

rows.grounds: one's own body as locus of contemplation

items.question: How should one ultimately identify one's own body in this practice?
premises: The preceding steps establish a specific visualization.
The form to be assumed is that of kāmakalā.
One's own body is the object of this identification.
items.inference: Therefore one should contemplate one's own body as the form of kāmakalā.
items.plain_english: Thus one should contemplate one's own body in the form of kāmakalā.

rows.grounds: highest practice pertaining to two types

items.question: What conduct concerning the two types will be explained next?
premises: The speaker announces a forthcoming explanation.
The explanation will be brief.
The subject is the supreme conduct of those two.
items.inference: Therefore the supreme conduct of those two will now be briefly described.
uncertainties: The identity of 'those two' depends on the immediate context.
items.plain_english: I shall briefly tell the supreme conduct of those two.

rows.grounds: assigned to divya and vīra grades

items.question: For which practitioner grades is this conduct prescribed or excluded?
premises: A specific practice is being identified.
The paśu grade is explicitly excluded.
The divine and hero grades are named as its domain.
items.inference: Therefore this practice belongs to the divine and hero, not to the paśu.
items.plain_english: O goddess, this practice is not for the paśu, but for the divine and the hero.

items.question: What ritual difficulty arises when wine and related substances are unavailable?
premises: A conditional case is introduced by fate.
Wine and similar substances are required items.
These substances may not be obtained.
items.inference: Therefore circumstances may arise in which wine and related substances cannot be obtained.
items.plain_english: O great goddess, if by fate wine and the other substances are not obtained.

items.question: What speech restriction applies when ritual substances are unavailable?
premises: The prior verse states substances may be unavailable.
A concessive response is given.
Declaring this sipping is explicitly prohibited.
items.inference: Therefore even in that case one must not speak of this sipping.
uncertainties: The ritual nuance of 'ācamanaṃ' in this context may be technical.
items.plain_english: Even so, O auspicious one, this sipping must not be spoken of.

rows.grounds: repeated for emphasis on daily practice

items.question: What regular practice is enjoined regarding wine and related substances?
premises: A conclusion is drawn from the preceding context.
Wine and related substances are the objects of practice.
The repetition 'day by day' indicates regularity.
items.inference: Therefore wine and related substances should be practiced daily.
items.plain_english: Therefore, O goddess, wine and the other substances should be used day after day.

rows.grounds: ritual placement specific to kaula practice
injunction to carry out the rite

items.question: What prerequisite and ritual action are required for kaula nyāsa?
premises: Initiation by a guru is stated as a prior condition.
The practitioner must have become initiated.
The kaula nyāsa is prescribed as the action.
items.inference: Therefore one initiated by a guru should perform the kaula nyāsa.
items.plain_english: Having been initiated by the guru, one should perform the kaula nyāsa.

rows.grounds: teaching previously declared by the speaker
refers to the previously stated teaching
injunction to carry out the rite

items.question: How must the two consecrations taught earlier be performed?
premises: The teaching was previously spoken by the speaker.
Two consecrations are specified.
Proper sequence is emphasized.
items.inference: Therefore one should perform the pair of consecrations in the proper order.
items.plain_english: One should perform that pair of consecrations, as spoken by me, in due order.

rows.grounds: determined by one's action or capacity

items.question: What determines whether divine yoga or hero yoga should be undertaken?
premises: Divine yoga is presented as an option.
Hero yoga is presented as an alternative option.
The choice follows accordance with action.
items.inference: Therefore one should undertake divine or hero yoga according to one's action.
uncertainties: The scope of 'karman' here may include prior action or present capacity.
items.plain_english: One should undertake either divine yoga or hero yoga, according to one's action.

rows.grounds: introduces the subject of the claim
refers back to the divine one
strong identification with Viṣṇu and denial of doubt

items.question: What exalted identity is claimed for one who is truly divine?
premises: The subject is one who is divine.
That one is emphatically identified as Viṣṇu.
The text denies any doubt about this claim.
items.inference: Therefore the truly divine one is declared to be Viṣṇu without doubt.
items.plain_english: Whoever is truly divine is indeed Viṣṇu; there is no doubt here.

rows.grounds: presence of a person in that place

items.question: Whose presence in a place confers special spiritual significance?
premises: A place is considered where a person dwells.
That person may be of the divine grade.
Alternatively that person may be the best of heroes.
items.inference: Therefore the dwelling of a divine or foremost hero marks a significant place.
items.plain_english: In whatever place a divine person or the best of heroes dwells.

items.question: What spatial extent is declared a field of siddhi around such a being?
premises: The place is designated as a field of siddhi.
This designation is explicitly declared.
Its extent is ten yojanas on all sides.
items.inference: Therefore the area for ten yojanas around is declared a field of siddhi.
items.plain_english: That place is declared a field of siddhi for ten yojanas on all sides.

rows.grounds: rarity of attaining this state or presence

items.question: How rare is the yoginī's presence even among powerful beings?
premises: The yoginī is the subject of rarity.
Even this is said to be hard to obtain.
Ḍākinīs and serpents are mentioned in relation to that rarity.
items.inference: Therefore the yoginī is exceedingly rare, even for ḍākinīs and serpents.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of the instrumental plurals is compressed and somewhat ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Even this yoginī is hard to obtain, even for ḍākinīs and serpents.

items.question: Which other classes of beings still find this presence difficult to obtain?
premises: Guhyakas and dānavas are included among those considered.
Mārīs, yakṣas, and kinnaras are also included.
Māyās are added to the list.
items.inference: Therefore many classes of powerful beings likewise find this presence hard to obtain.
uncertainties: The term 'māyābhiḥ' may refer to beings or powers; taken here as beings/powers.
items.plain_english: It is hard to obtain even for guhyakas, dānavas, mārīs, yakṣas, kinnaras, and māyās.

rows.grounds: growth and flourishing of the locality

items.question: What beneficial effects necessarily arise in the place of such a being?
premises: The location in question is that sanctified place.
Auspiciousness is said to arise there.
Prosperity of that city is also affirmed.
items.inference: Therefore that place certainly experiences auspiciousness and civic prosperity.
items.plain_english: Certainly there is auspiciousness there and prosperity for that city.

items.question: What continual manifestation of sacred knowledge occurs in that place?
premises: All scriptures are the subject of manifestation.
They shine forth in that context.
This manifestation occurs constantly.
items.inference: Therefore all scriptures continually shine forth there.
uncertainties: The force of 'sarvasmādapi' is syntactically compressed.
items.plain_english: All scriptures shine forth constantly, in every respect.
